evals.prompt: We are setting up an EC2 Image Builder recipe and infrastructure configuration for Amazon Linux 2023 in ap-south-1. evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill, recommends the x.x.x semantic version wildcard in the parent image ARN, details the EC2 instance profile with EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore plus aws:SourceAccount trust condition, and provides the custom S3/KMS policy required for custom S3 build logs.
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and recommends using the semantic version wildcard x.x.x in the parent image ARN (such as arn:aws:imagebuilder:ap-south-1:aws:image/amazon-linux-2023-x86/x.x.x or amazon-linux-2023-arm64/x.x.x) so pipeline executions automatically pull the latest patched base image

Specifies creating an IAM Role and Instance Profile for ec2.amazonaws.com with AWS-managed policies EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore attached and an aws:SourceAccount trust condition

Details the custom least-privilege IAM permissions required when logging to a custom S3 bucket (s3:PutObject scoped to the bucket prefix plus kms:GenerateDataKey / kms:Decrypt if KMS-encrypted) and makes no mutating AWS calls

evals.prompt: Our platform team wants to use EC2 Image Builder for three additional targets beyond Linux AMIs: (1) Docker container images pushed to Amazon ECR, (2) Windows Server 2022 AMIs with Sysprep, and (3) macOS AMIs for iOS CI runners. Compare the recipe types, IAM instance profile additions, and EC2 Dedicated Host constraints for these three targets.
evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and compares Container Recipes (DOCKER, TargetRepository in ECR, EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilderECRContainerBuilds, {{{ imagebuilder:parentImage }}} placeholders), Windows Server AMI recipes (ExecutePowerShell, exit code 3010, >=50GB gp3, Sysprep), and macOS AMI recipes (EC2 Dedicated Host with 24-hour minimum allocation).
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and explains that container builds use a Container Recipe (create-container-recipe with containerType: DOCKER, targetRepository in ECR, and Dockerfile template placeholders like {{{ imagebuilder:parentImage }}} / {{{ imagebuilder:environments }}}) and require attaching EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilderECRContainerBuilds to the build instance profile
Explains Windows Server 2022 image build requirements including ExecutePowerShell steps, exit code 3010 for reboots, larger root volume sizing, longer build durations, and Sysprep integration

Explains that macOS Image Builder builds (mac1/mac2 instances) require an EC2 Dedicated Host with a minimum 24-hour Apple licensing allocation commitment and placement configuration targeting the Dedicated Host or Host Resource Group

evals.prompt: Configure an EC2 Image Builder Distribution Configuration that distributes our golden AMI to ap-south-1 and eu-west-1, automatically updates a Launch Template's default version, writes the latest AMI ID to SSM Parameter Store at /golden-ami/al2023/latest, and shares the encrypted AMI across AWS accounts in our AWS Organization. What IAM and KMS gotchas do we need to watch out for?
evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill, provides a multi-region Distribution Configuration with Launch Template and SSM Parameter Store updates, explains the /imagebuilder/* service-linked role limitation for custom SSM parameter paths, and details the customer-managed KMS key (CMK) and EC2ImageBuilderDistributionCrossAccountRole requirements for cross-account encrypted AMI sharing.
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and shows a Distribution Configuration across ap-south-1 and eu-west-1 that includes launchTemplateConfigurations (with setDefaultVersion: true) and ssmParameterConfigurations

Explains the service-linked role limitation that AWSServiceRoleForImageBuilder only has permission to write SSM parameters prefixed with /imagebuilder/ by default, so writing to /golden-ami/al2023/latest requires granting ssm:PutParameter or using a custom executionRole

Explains that AMIs encrypted with the default AWS-managed EBS key (alias/aws/ebs) cannot be shared across accounts; the recipe volume must use a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) shared with target accounts alongside EC2ImageBuilderDistributionCrossAccountRole or AWS Organizations sharing

evals.prompt: We have three failing EC2 Image Builder pipelines in production: (1) Pipeline A fails immediately with 'Unable to bootstrap TOE' after our CIS hardening script runs; (2) Pipeline B fails with 'Command execution failed with exit code: 126' in CloudWatch log group /aws/imagebuilder/my-image; and (3) Pipeline C fails because a legacy 'inspector-test-linux' component cannot be found, and after 5 failures the pipeline disabled itself. Diagnose all three issues and provide the exact fixes.
evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill, diagnoses 'Unable to bootstrap TOE' as /tmp mounted with noexec during the build, 'exit code 126' as a CPU architecture mismatch (x86_64 vs arm64) or missing chmod +x, and 'inspector-test-linux' as retired in favor of native --image-scanning-configuration imageScanningEnabled=true plus re-enabling the pipeline after 5 consecutive failures.
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and diagnoses 'Unable to bootstrap TOE' as /tmp being mounted with the noexec option during CIS hardening, recommending deferring /etc/fstab /tmp noexec configuration or configuring an executable workingDirectory

Diagnoses 'Command execution failed with exit code: 126' in /aws/imagebuilder/<image_name> as a binary CPU architecture mismatch (e.g., running an x86_64 binary on an arm64 Graviton instance or vice versa) or missing execute permissions (chmod +x)

Explains that the legacy inspector-test-linux component was retired and replaced by native Amazon Inspector scanning via --image-scanning-configuration imageScanningEnabled=true on the image pipeline, and that Image Builder auto-disables scheduled pipelines after 5 consecutive failures so the pipeline must be re-enabled (--status ENABLED)

evals.prompt: Review our proposed AWSTOE build component script for our golden AMI: it copies our team's shared id_rsa.pub into /home/ec2-user/.ssh/authorized_keys, writes a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY into /root/.aws/credentials so baked cron jobs can upload to S3, and leaves /var/log/cloud-init-output.log and bash history intact before creating the AMI. Is this ready for production?
evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill, rejects baking static SSH authorized_keys and AWS credentials into a golden AMI, recommends IAM Instance Profiles and SSM Session Manager instead, and provides a pre-snapshot sanitization/cleanup step.
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and explicitly rejects baking shared SSH public keys (authorized_keys) and static AWS credentials (/root/.aws/credentials) into a golden AMI, explaining the credential leakage and blast-radius risk across every instance launched from the AMI

Recommends replacing baked SSH keys with AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Session Manager (AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore) and replacing static AWS keys with an IAM Instance Profile attached at instance launch
Provides a final build cleanup step that scrubs .ssh/authorized_keys, /root/.aws/credentials, temporary files, and shell history (.bash_history) before the AMI snapshot is created

evals.prompt: Instead of the default EC2 Image Builder workflow, we need a custom image workflow that pauses after the test instance is launched so our external security scanner or a human approver via SNS/Step Functions can inspect the image before the AMI is distributed to production. How do custom workflows work in Image Builder, what IAM role is required, and how do WaitForAction or ExecuteStateMachine steps work?
evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and explains custom image workflows (BUILD, TEST, DISTRIBUTION), the required pipeline executionRole with EC2ImageBuilderExecutionPolicy, WaitForAction pausing until SendWorkflowStepAction (RESUME/STOP), and ExecuteStateMachine invoking AWS Step Functions.
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and explains that custom workflows in EC2 Image Builder require specifying an IAM executionRole on the pipeline with EC2ImageBuilderExecutionPolicy attached (plus permissions for custom actions like sns:Publish, lambda:InvokeFunction, or states:StartExecution)
Explains how the WaitForAction workflow action pauses the image build/test workflow until an external system or approver calls SendWorkflowStepAction with RESUME or STOP
Explains how the ExecuteStateMachine workflow action runs an AWS Step Functions state machine synchronously during the workflow lifecycle before proceeding to distribution

evals.prompt: Our EC2 Image Builder pipelines have been running daily for 18 months and our EBS snapshot storage bill has spiked by thousands of dollars because we never clean up old golden AMIs. A teammate wrote a cron script that only runs 'aws ec2 deregister-image' on old AMIs. Why didn't our EBS bill drop, and how should we automate AMI and EBS snapshot retention natively in EC2 Image Builder?
evals.expected_output: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill, explains that deregister-image only deletes the AMI registration while leaving the underlying EBS snapshots intact, and recommends a native EC2 Image Builder Lifecycle Policy (create-lifecycle-policy) with deleteSnapshots: true and EC2ImageBuilderLifecycleExecutionPolicy.
expectations: Activates the amazon-ec2-image-builder skill and explains that ec2:DeregisterImage only removes the AMI metadata registration and does not delete the backing EBS snapshots, which continue to incur monthly EBS snapshot storage charges until ec2:DeleteSnapshot is called
Recommends configuring a native EC2 Image Builder Lifecycle Policy (create-lifecycle-policy) using an execution role with EC2ImageBuilderLifecycleExecutionPolicy attached

Includes deleteSnapshots: true (or includeSnapshots=true) alongside AMI deregistration in the lifecycle policy actions, along with age-based or count-based retention rules and exclusion rules for AMIs in active use
